-ka: -k-a — the -k of the genitive -ak 'of' (shown only before a vowel) followed by the locative -a 'in, at'; as in e₂-an-na-ka 'in the House of Heaven'
mes-ki-aĝ₂-ga-še-ir: Meskiaggasher (Langdon Mes-ki-em-ga-še-ir) — first king of Uruk (Eanna), son of the sun-god Utu; the third sign is AĜ₂ (NINDA₂×NE), which Langdon reads em; a Nippur copy spells the name Mes-ki-in-ga-še-ir
utu: Utu, the sun-god — written with the divine determinative and the UD sign (Langdon ᵈBabbar, whom he renders 'Shamash')
en: lord; also a priestly title ('high priest', Langdon); also the first element of royal names such as Enmerkar
ab-ba: sea (more usually a-ab-ba), or father (also 'elder') — two words spelled alike; Langdon takes the sea to be the Persian Gulf
ku₄: to enter — written with the TU sign (Langdon tur, 'penetrated'), read ku₄ today
ḫur-saĝ: mountain range, the highlands (Langdon ĝar-sag); the first sign is the diamond-shaped ḪAR/ḪUR, so it is read ḫur by sign
en-me-kar: Enmerkar (Langdon En-me-kar; a Nippur copy has En-me-ir-kar) — king of Uruk, son of Meskiaggasher, the builder of Uruk; EN-ME-KAR
unug: Uruk (Langdon Unug, Erech) — city in southern Babylonia, the seat of this dynasty; written with the UNUG sign (AB-gunû) plus the place-determinative KI (unread), as unug{ki}
-ga: genitive -a(k) 'of', written -ga after a final g (unug{ki}-ga 'of Uruk')
du₃: to build — written with the KAK sign (Langdon dū)
lugal-banda₃: Lugalbanda (Langdon ᵈLugal-banda(da)) — king of Uruk, shepherd, later deified; lugal 'king' + banda₃, written with the TUR sign and followed by DA, a phonetic complement that is not read separately
dumu-zi: Dumuzi (Langdon ᵈDumu-zi) — king of Uruk, later deified; dumu (TUR) + zi; Langdon identifies him with an older dying god Ab-ú
šu-ḪA.GUNU: fisherman (Langdon) — ŠU + ḪA-gunû, a variant of the 'fish' sign ḪA with added strokes; the usual word is šu-ku₆; how this form was read is uncertain, so the sign is given by name
ḫa-a: Ḫaa (Langdon Ḫa-bûr; usually Kuara today) — a town, Dumuzi's city; written ḪA + A with the place-determinative KI; Langdon's bûr is the A sign, read a by sign
{d}gibil-ga-mes: Gilgamesh (Langdon ᵈGibil-ga-meš) — king of Uruk, lord of Kullab, later a deified hero; written with the divine determinative, GIŠ.BIL, GA and MES (Langdon meš); the identification of the BIL sign is uncertain
lil₂-la₂: lillu — Langdon 'a fool' (Akkadian lillu; lil-lá in his transliteration), KID + LAL; lil₂ is also 'wind, phantom', so the sense is uncertain
kul-aba₄: Kullab (Langdon Kullab) — a district of Uruk; written KUL + AB
-ba-ke₄: genitive -a(k) 'of', written -ba after a final b, + ergative -e, written with the KID sign (Langdon -ge); marks a phrase such as 'lord of Kullab' as the subject of the clause
ur-{d}nun-gal: Urnungal (Langdon Ur-ᵈNun-gal) — king of Uruk, son of Gilgamesh; ur 'man, servant' + the god Nungal, 'servant of Nungal'; another copy writes Ur-ᵈNun-lugal
utul-kalam-ma: Utulkalamma (Langdon Utul-kalam-ma) — king of Uruk, son of Urnungal; the first sign is one compound sign U+GUD, kept as Langdon's utul, and its reading is uncertain; kalam 'the land' + -ma (genitive -a(k) after m)
la-ba-še-ir: Labašer (Langdon La-ba-še-ir, 'Labasher') — king of Uruk; LA-BA-ŠE-IR
en-nun-dara₃-an-na: Ennundaraanna (Langdon En-nun-nad-an-na) — king of Uruk; en 'lord' + nun 'prince' + a third sign + an-na 'of heaven'; the third sign is a first identification as DARA₃ (Langdon reads nad), so uncertain
[…]-ḫe₂-de₃: […]-ḫede — king of Uruk; only the end of the name is known, the first sign being broken away (Langdon leaves it '?'); ḫe₂ is GAN (Langdon ĝe), and de₃ is NE (Langdon de), an uncertain identification
me-lam-an-na: Melamanna — king of Uruk; me-lam 'awe-inspiring radiance' + an-na 'of heaven'
lugal-ki-aĝ₂: Lugalkiaĝ (Langdon Lugal-ki-aga) — last king of the first dynasty of Uruk; lugal 'king' + ki + AĜ₂ (Langdon aga); ki—aĝ₂ is the verb 'to love'; the identification of the third sign and the sense of the name are uncertain
urim₂: Ur — city in southern Babylonia (written ŠEŠ.AB plus place-determinative KI, as urim₂{ki}; Langdon Uri)

__broaden__.ba-an-: ba-n- — verbal prefix chain: ba- (often of motion away, or a middle/passive sense) + -n-, which ordinarily marks a 'he' who acts · with a verb of entering (ba-an-ku₄) the -n- may point to the place entered rather than a doer; the grammar is uncertain
